content:
jasper: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a concrete plan for attribution when requests are proxied/batched across tenants. Current gap: billing needs deterministic credit ownership, audits need lineage for disputed charges.

maria: agree. two quick options: (A) attach a request-level owner header and do best-effort token attribution, or (B) emit per-token attribution events to the audit stream.

lee: option B gives full proof but is heavy. per-token events -> 4-10x event volume depending on prompt length. increases cost and storage.

jasper: right — we can't blow up the event pipeline. can we hybridize? lightweight fast-path + heavyweight audit envelope on decision points?

alex: propose design: emit a compact "charge record" for every response with fields: request_id, tenant_id, token_count, model_variant, primary_owner. Then asynchronously materialize token-level lineage only when a) charge exceeds threshold, b) customer disputes, or c) flagged by sampling.

sophia: that maps to compliance: audits rarely need full token trace for every request, but we must be able to reconstruct it deterministically when asked. key is reproducible mapping from request -> token sequence + owner.

maria: implementation notes: persist minimal seed (prompt_hash, model_version, random_seed, partial_kv_snapshot_ref). For replay, the replay job will re-run inference in a locked environment to regenerate exact token boundaries. this avoids streaming per-token events live.

lee: downside: replay needs pinned model binary & quantization params. must record exact runtime kernel/profile. add `runtime_fingerprint` to envelope.

alex: agree. example envelope (compact):

```
{
  "request_id": "r_123",
  "tenant": "acme",
  "tokens": 482,
  "model": "redwood-7b-v2-q4",
  "primary_owner": "tenant",
  "seed_refs": ["s3://kv-snaps/2026/03/01/snap-42"],
  "runtime_fingerprint": "gpu-rt-0xafe23"
}
```

jasper: nice. operationally we need: 1) fast ingest path for compact envelopes, 2) archive for seeds/snapshots, 3) replay worker pool with pinned models, 4) audit API to materialize lineage on demand.

sophia: also think about retention & privacy: keep seeds + snapshots encrypted and TTLed per contract. enterprise customers can opt for longer retention and on-prem snapshots.

maria: open question: how to handle multi-tenant batched requests where a single GPU call returns interleaved tokens? who owns the shared KV cache prefixes?

lee: suggestion: attribute tokens to the original request_id and persist an ordered mapping of (request_id, token_offset, token_count). When batching, the runtime must emit an assignment map back to the fast-path. keeps attribution deterministic without extra per-token events.

alex: that mapping is small (per-request offsets) and scales with number of requests, not tokens. good win.

jasper: ok action items: maria to draft an RFC for compact envelope + replay pipeline; lee to design assignment-map schema and runtime hook; sophia to list compliance retention matrix per tier; alex to sketch cost model (ingest/storage/replay). I'll open a tracking ticket.

audit-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1427: "Attribution: compact-envelope + on-demand token lineage" (assigned jasper, due 2026-04-10).

jasper: thanks — quick thumbs? :thumbsup:

maria: :thumbsup:

lee: :thumbsup: will start proto this week.

alex: posting a short perf test plan in the ticket.

sophia: adding compliance matrix entries now.

jasper: great. we'll sync in engineering sync on Friday for rollout cadence.
